description: Reasoning vault aligned with OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.4: evaluate and build compositions, compose in either order, simplify formulas, and determine the domain of a composite.

archetypes.name: Evaluate a Composite Function
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.4 — Composition of Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: In (f∘g)(x), the output of g becomes the input of f; the inner function acts first.
archetypes.mentalModel: Pass the original input through g, then feed that output into f.

cognitiveTraps.description: Applying the outer function first and evaluating g(f(x)) instead of f(g(x)).
Reporting g(x) without applying the outer function.

archetypes.figureNone: This archetype is exact symbolic substitution; a diagram would not add information needed to find the value.

archetypes.name: Build and Simplify a Composite Rule
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.4 — Create a New Function by Composition of Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A composite rule is formed by substituting the entire inner expression wherever the outer rule's input appears, then simplifying while preserving grouping.
archetypes.mentalModel: Replace the outer input with one grouped copy of the inner output; simplify only after the replacement is complete.

cognitiveTraps.description: Substituting the inner expression into only part of the outer rule or dropping its parentheses.
Using the reverse order when composing two functions.

archetypes.figureNone: The target is algebraic substitution and simplification rather than a graph-reading task.

archetypes.name: Determine the Domain of a Composite
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.4 — Domain of a Composite Function
archetypes.coreConcept: An input is allowed only when it belongs to the inner function's domain and its inner output belongs to the outer function's domain.
archetypes.mentalModel: Check both gates in order: x must be legal for g, then g(x) must be legal as an input to f.

cognitiveTraps.description: Checking only the outer rule's restriction and forgetting the inner function's own domain.
Checking x in Dom(g) but not checking whether g(x) is allowed by f.
Including an endpoint allowed by the inner radical even though it makes the outer reciprocal undefined.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: x=1 \text{ included although } g(x)=0 \text{ enters a denominator}

archetypes.figureNone: The domain is found by intersecting algebraic restrictions; plotting it would disclose the excluded values.
